newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps sees CFDs revisit earlier weakness.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps sees CFDs revisit earlier weakness.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady to a touch weaker on Monday in thinnish trading activity.
Brent CFDs ended broadly steady having firmed a few cents after earlier weakness, heavy fuel lost up to $1 while gasoline and naphtha were effectively unchanged.
Brent CFDs picked up a few cents with June 16-20 rising to around -56 cents against August Brent compared with earlier in the day, but steady against Friday.

June 23-27 was one or two cents higher at -48/49 cents against August Brent compared with Friday while June 30-July 4 also gained a couple of cents to -44 cents. July 7-July 11 was pegged around -39 cents.

Dealers said CFDs had been weaker for much of the day, but activity and levels picked up towards the end of business. June 23-27 traded at -50 cents and -53 cents and June 24-30 was done at -45 cents.

Heavy fuel lost a touch under $1 with July trading at $83 during the day and subsequently heard offered at $83. There was talk of a morning July trade at $84, but this was treated cautiously by some traders. August also traded at $83 while 3Q97 went at $84.

The strong buying of wet gasoline seen last week continued on Monday with as high as $194 done on barges. Swaps appeared resistant to the firmer wet numbers with July hovering unchanged around $185 with August pretty much flat with a hint of backwardation. The June/July gasoline spread was heard offered at $8, but there were no bids.

Naphtha also languished with only a couple of private deals done around Friday's numbers. Dealers said July was valued at $180 with August marginally in contango by up to 50 cents and September flat with July.
Jet swaps were holding around $19 for July and 4Q was done twice at $26.
